author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it by full name, on one unpaged page reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when GET /specialties.html is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name on a single page with no pagination
given a specialty held by veterinarians, when the specialty directory is opened, then each of them is listed under it by first name then last name, such as "Helen Leary"
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian is listed under no specialty
given a veterinarian holding several specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian is listed under each of them (PRD edge case 1)
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the specialty directory is opened, then it is still listed and shown as held by none rather than left blank (PRD edge case 2)
given the specialty directory, when it is rendered, then specialties and the veterinarians under each appear in a stable order (PRD edge case 3)
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties (NG-2, unchanged per the intake decision)
Any navigation entry or link from another page to the specialty directory (intake decision: reachable by its URL alone; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request)
A machine-readable form of the specialty list (REQ-VET-002 was withdrawn as an artifact; nothing asked for one)
Searching or filtering by specialty (NG-9 keeps search to owners; this page is a static listing with no query input)

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Read-only page inside the existing vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure, § Contracts). Adjustments: (1) a SpecialtyRepository for the existing Specialty lookup, following the PetTypeRepository precedent of a name-ordered query, because unheld specialties (PRD edge case 2) are unreachable from VetRepository; (2) an immutable SpecialtyDirectory record built by a pure static factory from the ordered specialties and VetRepository.findAll() (cached), per architecture-principles § Logic Placement (a change of representation leaves the controller) and § Building Blocks (value object = record, List.copyOf); (3) a SpecialtyController serving GET /specialties.html, which binds nothing, delegates to the two repositories and the factory, and selects vets/specialtyList (catalog row Web controller). Ordering (edge case 3): specialties by name then id in the query; holders by last name, then first name, then id inside the factory; full name composed first-name space last-name. A specialty with no holders yields an empty list that the template renders with the existing 'none' key, mirroring vetList.html. The template uses fragments/layout with a menu argument matching no nav item, so the site navigation (REQ-SYS-001) renders and no entry is added (edge case 4). Existing keys 'specialties', 'vets', 'none' may cover the wording; any new key goes in all eleven bundles (REQ-LANG-002, I18nPropertiesSyncTest). No Vet-to-Specialty back-reference is added; Vet stays the owning side. Basis: grep and file reads (IDE oracle not connected): VetRepository.java, Vet.java, Specialty.java, PetTypeRepository.java, BaseEntity.java (no equals/hashCode), templates/vets/vetList.html, templates/fragments/layout.html.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html binds no request input: no parameter, path variable, or form object; binding target is none (security-principles § Trust Boundaries; Threat Model XSS row relies on Thymeleaf default escaping of stored names, so no th:utext).

Boundary: SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository in SpecialtyControllerTests: hand-written doubles registered through a @TestConfiguration under @WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class); SpecialtyRepository declares one method on Spring Data Repository (not JpaRepository) so the double stays one method (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: hand-write mocks).
Boundary: SpecialtyDirectoryTests is a plain unit test over real Vet and Specialty instances with ids set; no double.
Boundary: the ordered specialty query is exercised against the embedded database through the existing @DataJpaTest ClinicServiceTests (real implementation, seed data), asserting name order.
Boundary: HTTP transport via MockMvc, the one sanctioned framework harness (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).

patterns.description: name-ordered JPQL lookup query; mirror it, adding id as the tie-break
full-name composition and the 'none' fallback for an empty specialty set

risks.risk: Matching holders by object identity or equals fails: BaseEntity overrides neither, and the cached vets and the freshly queried specialties are distinct instances, so every specialty would show as held by none.
risks.mitigation: Match by Specialty id inside the factory (system-design § Contracts invariant note); SpecialtyDirectoryTests builds the specialties and the vets' specialties as separate instances sharing an id.

risks.risk: Specialty directory path scales with specialties x veterinarians (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty directory row).
risks.mitigation: Bounded per the row: simplest readable form, one ordered query plus the cached vet list, inverted with a Stream pipeline in memory; no pagination, no extra query per specialty.

risks.risk: Equal names make an order non-deterministic (PRD edge case 3).
risks.mitigation: Id tie-break for specialties in the query and for holders in the factory comparator (Comparator.comparing chain).

risks.risk: Lazy access after the transaction closes, since open-in-view is disabled (system-design § Persistence).
risks.mitigation: Vet.specialties is already eager; the factory runs on loaded entities and the view reads only the record's strings.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log. Design writes to docs/system-design.md: Contracts rows for SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyController; REQ-VET-003 joined to Vet, Specialty, VetRepository; an invariant clause on identity matching; vet line in Package Structure; a new § Scale and Load section (absent before, added from the doctor template) with the specialty directory row. No ADR: the choices follow existing patterns and stay inside this slice. The prd-entry file_targets name VetController and VetControllerTests; the design places the page on its own SpecialtyController (one HTTP surface per controller, Naming row 'prefixed by the surface it serves'), so the six test_names live in SpecialtyControllerTests and VetController stays unchanged. Holder order (last name, first name, id) is this design's narrowest stable choice; the PRD mandates only stability. Owner absent: no question was left that the decisions do not answer.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Widening the exposed surface (security-principles row): one new GET route, SpecialtyController.java:39 `@GetMapping("/specialties.html")`, read-only, exposing only specialty names and vet full names already public on the vets page; the change states its exposure in the system-design SpecialtyController row ('binds no request input'). No management-exposure change (application.properties:21 `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=*` is the pre-existing baseline, not in the diff).

Mass assignment and request binding: the handler signature `String showSpecialtyDirectory(Model model)` (SpecialtyController.java:40) binds no @ModelAttribute, @RequestBody, @RequestParam, or @PathVariable, so no binder allow-list is needed and no persisted type is bound from the request.

Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository.java uses a static JPQL `@Query("SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name, specialty.id")` with no parameters and no concatenation; the repository is read-only (`@Transactional(readOnly = true)`) and extends Repository, not CrudRepository, so it exposes no write methods.

Cross-site scripting: specialtyList.html renders stored names only through escaping `th:text` (`${specialty.name}`, `${holderName}`); `grep -n 'utext\|__\${'` on the template returned no match, so no unescaped output or Thymeleaf preprocessing is introduced.

Error disclosure and fail-secure: Vet.java:47 `@ManyToMany(fetch = FetchType.EAGER)` loads specialties with the cached vets, so with `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` (application.properties:11) the in-memory inversion raises no lazy-initialization exception into the message-rendering error page; the change adds no exception messages, logging, or System.out.

Resource management: the unpaged page inverts the cached full vet list in memory; the system-design Scale and Load row records the data set as bounded with no application write path, so no unbounded request-driven allocation is introduced. SpecialtyDirectory is an immutable record (List.copyOf in both canonical constructors) and the controller singleton holds only final repository references, so no shared mutable state.
Secrets: the diff adds no credential, token, password, key, or connection string (read across all changed production files and docs hunks).

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set and no dependency is added; no NVD match runs in this review (no dependency-check plugin, a standing gap listed in docs/security-principles.md § Standing Gaps). Resolved versions from `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath`: Spring Boot 4.1.2, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, jackson-databind 3.1.7.
